paper.title_en: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
paper.abstract_en: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $α_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schrödinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.
